summary: Pipeline tooling under tools/nightly/ that the nightly run puts around the unchanged image: a run-scoped certificate authority and a price stand-in answering the providers' real names, a one-way relay, source checks, prepared vaults and backups made through the app's own browser code, a dating-back patch, and an MCP server that is qa's only way to the server. It is never in the image.

read.role: Nightly and stable is the requirement this feature serves: shards on a network of their own with no route out, the stand-in under the real source names, the vaults made with the app's own browser code, qa reaching the server only through harness tools, and nothing of the harness in the image

Tech stack, Packaging: the image holds nothing of the harness. Status codes: the stand-in's statuses are the providers' own and outside this set. Application hardening: the session, the sign-in limits each shard spends and the egress rules the stand-in is trusted under. Vault epoch: the X-Solvent-Vault header every vault request the generator sends carries
the composition known_table must equal exactly, the seeded currency list prices.py must equal, the constants that name no setting, and the breaker that app_stop and app_start reset
the expected figures prepare computes independently: latest quantity times price, assets and debts, archived and unpriced holdings excluded
the rate records the script writes, the proposals it passes to refreshPrices, the price as recorded, and editedRatePayload
the snapshot records written, and the same-date pair the plan plants
holdings with their units and the archive date the archived-holding coverage depends on
the AAD under which the damaged record is encrypted for another record_id
GET /api/export with the X-Solvent-Request header, the backup file shape, formatVersion and kdf envelope, and why a format-1 fixture is never regenerated

sections: Bootstrap: the first administrator, and the locked-out one
read.role: the administrator invite minted through the CLI and --force, the invites made through POST /api/admin/invites, and the status the expired one carries
what /register?invite= does, so fixtures.mjs registers as the page does
/api/auth/upgrade-kdf for the older vault, and the session's absolute 12-hour expiry the aged session is dated past
saveProfile's record, the idleLockMinutes the idle-lock-out-of-range vault stores and how the app reads an out-of-range one, and the session the aged cookie belongs to
SECRET_KEY, the writable volume and the tables patch.py touches, and the Dockerfile and .dockerignore criteria that keep tools out of the image

location.value: tools/nightly/, pipeline tooling, never in the image. Standard library only, Python 3.12 or later and Node 24 or later. No script adds a dependency. Imports beyond those are exactly the ones in imports

value.allowed: the standard library and node: built-ins, plus exactly these
value.prices: standin.py, mcp.py and prices.py prepare import prices, their sibling in tools/nightly/, on the path as the running script's own directory. Every price comes from that one module
value.solventRates: sources.py imports from solvent.rates the constants rate-lookup.md names for it, in tonight's image with PYTHONPATH=/app
value.cdp: fixtures.mjs imports tests/browser/cdp.mjs, the Chrome driver, rather than keeping a second one
value.nothingElse: nothing else imports from solvent or tests/. Nothing in solvent imports from tools/, and the harness's own tests are the only code outside it that does

scriptExitCodes.condition: a script that runs to an end. No script writes anything but its stated outputs

imageUnderTest.value: tonight's image, unchanged. Every harness container runs it with its entrypoint overridden and tools/nightly/ mounted read-only. No step builds, commits or tags an image

harnessContainerFlags.value: --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges:true on every harness container

value.nightly: created with --internal: the app, the stand-in and one leg of the relay, nothing on it has a route out
value.nightly-edge: an ordinary bridge: the relay's other leg, publishing 127.0.0.1:8000

standinAliases.condition: network aliases of the stand-in on nightly, so Docker's resolver answers the providers' real names with its address

value.noRouteOut: the app's only network is internal, so a lookup reaches the stand-in or nothing
value.trustByNameAndMount: the stand-in is trusted by name and by a mounted trust store holding only the run's CA over the image's system store, never by a setting
value.caScope: the CA vouches for the two provider names alone, for one day, and signs once. Its key is deleted as soon as the stand-in's certificate is signed, and it is name-constrained
value.qaOnlyThroughTools: the tools have fixed names and argument shapes, take no command, path, container name or URL as an argument, and run with an empty environment, so no token reaches them. The walk step holds no unrestricted shell
value.serverTextIsUntrusted: the log and the request list return to qa as JSON strings, never interpreted
value.fixturePasswordsArePublic: committed in the plan, they open only throwaway vaults on an instance nobody outside the runner can reach, and are never reused
value.preparedDataStaysOnRunner: the output directory and the TLS directory are never uploaded as artifacts

command.value: python3 tools/nightly/ca.py <dir>, running the openssl command line with argument lists and never a shell. <dir> must be empty or absent

value.trust/<subject hash>.0: ca.pem again, named by openssl x509 -subject_hash

caPrivateKey.value: exists only in a temporary directory deleted before the script exits, whether or not signing succeeded

nameConstraints.ca: critical, permitted DNS:api.frankfurter.dev and DNS:api.nbp.pl, excluded IP:0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 and IP:::/0

strictness.value: both conform to RFC 5280 as OpenSSL's X509_V_FLAG_X509_STRICT checks it, because the image's Python enables that flag in its default context and would otherwise refuse the stand-in

mount.value: trust/ read-only at /etc/ssl/certs in the app container, the image's OpenSSL CA directory

command.value: python /harness/standin.py --cert <leaf.pem> --key <leaf.key> --state <dir> [--port 443], in a container of tonight's image on nightly

server.value: HTTPS only, TLS 1.2 or later, a ThreadingHTTPServer behind ssl.SSLContext(PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER) holding the leaf alone. Routes on the Host header, and any other host gets 421 with an empty body

value.request: GET /v1/<D>?base=<Q>, Q a known currency, D on or after 1999-01-04
value.answer: 200, {"amount": 1.0, "base": Q, "date": <last publication day <= D>, "rates": {C: ...}} for every known C != Q

value.request: GET /api/cenyzlota/<S>/<E>?format=json, S <= E, span at most 93 days, a publication day in range
value.answer: 200, [{"data": <day>, "cena": ...}, ...], every publication day in range, ascending

value.request: same, no publication day in range
same, S > E or span over 93 days

failureModes.value: <state>/modes.json is {"frankfurter": "up" | "down", "nbp": "up" | "down"}, read on every request. Absent, unreadable or malformed, both sources are up. A source that is down answers every request 503 with an empty body, after recording it

value.writing: one line per request, appended before the answer is sent, the file opened, appended and closed under a lock per request
value.seq: counts from 1 and continues from the file's existing line count at start
value.targetAndHeaders: exactly as received, in order. headers is a list of [name, value] pairs
value.body: the received body decoded as Latin-1, up to 64 KiB
value.unparsableRequest: still a line, with what could be read and status as sent

home.value: prices.py is the one home of every price the stand-in publishes. A price is a pure function of the source, the date and the currency

publicationDays.value: Monday to Friday, no holidays, up to and including the stand-in's current UTC date. Frankfurter publishes from 1999-01-04 and NBP from 2013-01-02, the start of the real series the app calls and each symbol's date floor. The app sends no earlier date, so the stand-in's 404 before them is never exercised by it

currencies.value: Frankfurter's list, the same set as the seeded currency half of the symbol table, each with a reference value ref[C], units of C per euro, in a constant table in prices.py, with ref["EUR"] = 1

frankfurterFormula.value: for publication day p, base Q and symbol C != Q: rates[C] = ref[C] / ref[Q] x f(p), rounded half-even to 5 significant digits, where f(p) = 1 + ((p.toordinal() mod 101) - 50) / 2000

nbpFormula.value: for publication day p: cena = 250 x g(p), rounded half-even to 2 decimal places, where g(p) = 1 + ((p.toordinal() mod 89) - 44) / 1000

arithmetic.value: decimal.Decimal in the default context. A value is written into JSON as a number with exactly those digits, so the app's parse through float and str returns the same decimal

knownTable.value: prices.known_table(date, quote) is what /api/rates must answer for the whole table on that date and quote, without cached: every currency but quote, and XAU-g and XAU-ozt where NBP published within the 14-day window, each {rate, base, asOf, source}. It applies rate-lookup.md's composition exactly as pinned in Providers

relay.value: python /harness/relay.py --listen 0.0.0.0:8000 --to solvent:8000, in a container of tonight's image. It copies bytes both ways between each accepted connection and one new connection to the fixed target, closes both when either side closes, and reads, logs and alters nothing. It is the runner's only way to the app, and the app sees it as every client's peer

command.value: python /harness/sources.py check|probe, in a container of tonight's image with PYTHONPATH=/app, importing FX_URL, NBP_URL, USER_AGENT, EGRESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES and SEEDED_SYMBOLS from solvent.rates and opening each URL with the default context and redirects off, as the app does

request.value: one request to each source, for quote CHF and the date D seven days before the current UTC date (NBP from D - 14 days to D)

outputLine.value: <frankfurter|nbp> <ok|no-answer|changed> <reason>, one per source. The reason names the status, exception class or first shape violation, never the body

frankfurterShape.value: an object whose base is CHF, whose date is an ISO date within [D - 7 days, D], and whose rates maps three-letter upper-case codes to numbers above zero, every seeded currency but CHF among them. A boolean is not a number

nbpShape.value: a non-empty array, ascending by data, of objects whose data is an ISO date within [D - 14 days, D] and whose cena is a number above zero. A boolean is not a number

value.no-answer: name resolution, connection or TLS failure, a timeout, 429 or any 5xx
value.changed: any other status but 200, 3xx included because the app follows no redirect. A 200 body over the size cap, not JSON, or off the shape

checkRuns.value: once a night against the real sources, in the build job, on the default bridge network. Exits 1 when any source is changed and 0 otherwise. Its no-answer lines are the note in the run's summary

probeRuns.value: per shard against the stand-in, on nightly with trust/ mounted as in the app. Exits 0 only when both sources are ok and a TCP connection to 1.1.1.1:443 does not open within 3 seconds, which proves the trust store, the aliases and the missing route out together

coverageNames.condition: each must be covered by at least one prepared item, a test fails a plan that leaves one out, and prepare exits 1 naming it. What each item must be is stated in the plan table there

value.long-history: every month end from before 2013-01-02 through the last month end before today, holding the main currency, USD, XAU-g and a debt. Gold dates before 2013-01-02 carry a price typed by hand
value.many-dimension-values: a dimension with at least five values, each held by at least one holding
value.rate-edited-long-ago: a proposed rate more than five years back, edited to a figure other than the known price, and a holding whose latest quantity sits on that date
value.no-source-unit: a holding in XAG-ozt, priced by hand
value.own-unit: a holding in a unit outside the symbol table, priced by hand on one old date only
value.archived-holding: archived on a recording date at which every unit already has a price, so archiving makes no lookup
value.other-main-currency: a vault whose main currency is EUR
value.damaged-record: a snapshot encrypted under the AAD of another record_id, so it fails authentication
value.older-vault: the credential's KDF envelope has m = 32768 and is otherwise the default
value.idle-lock-out-of-range: a vault owner used for nothing else, whose profile record carries idleLockMinutes: 0, written through saveProfile although the Idle lock select does not offer it. The app reads it as five minutes
value.aged-session: issued 12 hours 5 minutes before patch.py ran and last active 1 minute before it
value.expired-invite: a vault-owner invite that expired one day before patch.py ran
value.current-backup: tonight's export of the long-history vault

planUniqueness.value: neither the damaged record nor the pair is its holding's latest quantity, and neither sits on a holding's archive date, so every expected total has exactly one correct value. Every other quantity, rate and setting in the plan is one the app's own screens could write, idle-lock-out-of-range's idleLockMinutes: 0 alone excepted

command.value: python3 tools/nightly/prices.py prepare <plan> <out>, expanding the plan against the current UTC date

value.<out>/script.json: per account, in order, every write the generator makes, with concrete dates, values and, for each proposed rate, the proposal from known_table
value.<out>/expected.json: per vault, and for each backup file, the expected figures under both pricing modes

expectedFigures.value: computed independently of the app in Decimal. Each active, priced holding's figure is its latest quantity times its price (the latest price, or the price as recorded), rounded half-even at scale 12, as static/js/decimal.js multiplies. The total is the sum of those at scale 12. assets sums the figures above zero and debts those below. Each is given as exact (scale 12 without trailing zeros) and display (rounded half-even to the places the vault's profile shows, no grouping, '-' for a negative). Archived holdings, holdings with no quantity and holdings with no price are listed by name under excluded, with the reason

dateReadOnce.value: prepare reads the date once and writes it as the manifest's today, and the expected figures hold for that date, since no later price is written

command.value: node tools/nightly/fixtures.mjs --base <url> --invite <path> --plan <plan> --out <dir>, with CHROME naming the browser. Reads <dir>/script.json and <dir>/expected.json

registration.value: accounts register through /register?invite= as the page does, one fresh Chrome profile per account. --invite is a CLI-minted administrator invite, which registers harness-admin. Every other invite is made through POST /api/admin/invites from that administrator's page, the expired one with the plan's label

writes.value: only through the served modules /static/js/session.js, writes.js, crypto.js and api.js: saveProfile, saveHolding, saveSnapshot, refreshPrices with the script's proposals, saveRate with editedRatePayload, and archiveHolding. The damaged record and the pair are the exceptions, written as tests/browser/harness.mjs plant writes. No record is written by the generator's own crypto

noLookup.value: proposals come from the script, so the generator sends nothing to /api/rates and spends no part of any limit

olderVault.value: rotated through /api/auth/upgrade-kdf with keys derived at m = 32768, as tests/browser/harness.mjs makeStale does, and patch.py then records that parameter

currentBackup.value: the body of GET /api/export, fetched by the page through api.js, so it carries the X-Solvent-Request header and the vault epoch

everyVaultRequestCarriesTheEpoch.value: every request the generator sends for a vault carries X-Solvent-Vault, the plant writes and makeStale's upgrade-kdf included. A request without it is a Bad Request from the gate and a replaced epoch a Conflict, so the generator, through api.js, holds the epoch registration or sign-in handed it

agedCookie.value: read with CDP Network.getCookies in that account's profile, right after it registers

value.storage-state.json: Playwright storage state, {"cookies": [<the aged session's cookie>], "origins": []}, with expires, httpOnly, secure and sameSite as CDP reported them

value.expected: keyed by username or backup file, each {latest, asRecorded}, each holding total, assets, debts, holdings (by name) and excluded (by name, with the reason). Every figure is {exact, display}
value.coverageRule: every coverage name appears under some covers, and qa reads nothing else to know what is prepared

command.value: python /harness/patch.py <database> <patches.json>, in a one-off container of tonight's image with --network none, the app's volume, and the app stopped

times.value: count back from patch.py's own clock and are written as the app writes them, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00

value: UPDATE sessions SET issued_at = ?, last_active_at = ? WHERE principal_id = (SELECT id FROM principals WHERE username = ?)
UPDATE invites SET created_at = ?, expires_at = ? WHERE label = ? AND status = 'pending'
UPDATE credentials SET params = json_set(params, '$.kdf.m', ?) WHERE principal_id = (SELECT id FROM principals WHERE username = ?) AND method = 'password'
statements.condition: these statements, with every value bound as a parameter, are all it runs, and it touches no other table

transaction.value: one transaction. A statement that changes no row, or a credential change to a value outside 8192 <= m < 65536, rolls it all back and exits 1. An unknown key exits 2 before anything is opened

connection.value: opens the file through sqlite3 with PRAGMA secure_delete = ON, as the app does

olderBackup.value: fixtures/backup-format-1.json was made once, by prepare and fixtures.mjs from backup-format-1.plan.json, at the server's default KDF envelope of that build, with every date absolute. It has formatVersion 1 and a kdf envelope at m = 65536, t = 3, p = 1. Its plan and expected files are kept and none of the three is ever regenerated. The manifest carries its password and points at it

command.value: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 tools/nightly/mcp.py --container solvent --state <dir> --url http://localhost:8000. An MCP server over stdio, JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line, no network listener

protocol.value: initialize answers with the protocolVersion the client sent, capabilities {tools: {}} and serverInfo {name: "harness"}. tools/list lists the tools below and nothing else. ping answers {}. Any other method is error -32601. Notifications get no reply

schemas.value: every tool's inputSchema sets additionalProperties: false. An argument outside its schema returns isError: true naming the argument, and does nothing. A result is one text content item holding a JSON document

docker.value: runs with an argument list, never a shell. The container name and the state directory come only from the server's own arguments

startCount.value: at start it records the request list's line count, and price_requests shows only requests after it

server_log.does: docker logs <container>, stderr merged into stdout
server_log.returns: {"lines": [...], "next": n}, at most 500 lines from line since

price_requests.returns: {"requests": [...], "next": seq}, at most 200 entries with seq above both since and the start count

price_source.arguments: source: frankfurter | nbp, state: up | down
price_source.does: writes modes.json through a temporary file and os.replace

known_prices.arguments: date: YYYY-MM-DD on or before today, quote: a known currency
known_prices.returns: the table, independent of the modes

app_start.does: docker start <container>, then polls <url>/login until it answers 200, at most 60 seconds

breakerReset.value: app_stop and app_start reset the app's circuit breaker, because it lives in process memory. app_start on a running container changes nothing and answers running

buildJob.value: after the image is built and before any shard starts, a step with the id sources runs sources.py check in a container of tonight's image on the default network, appends its output to the step summary, and fails the job on exit 1

4 start standin on nightly with both aliases, as the runner's own user, with --sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=443, tls/ and tools/nightly/ read-only and standin/ writable
5 start solvent on nightly alone, with the hardening it has today, a fresh SECRET_KEY, and tls/trust/ read-only at /etc/ssl/certs

shardSteps.condition: steps whose failure fails the shard as the harness

walkStep.value: passes tools/nightly/fixtures/out/manifest.json as the manifest, adds the harness MCP server and --storage-state tools/nightly/fixtures/out/storage-state.json to the Playwright server's arguments, allows mcp__harness and mcp__playwright and no Bash beyond gh issue list and gh issue view. On failure it prints docker logs of solvent and standin

owner.value: .github/workflows/nightly.yml is the client's. An agent cannot write it, so these requirements reach it as the exact change in the pull request and its comment on the issue (CLAUDE.md, When something fails)

value.sourceChanged: the build job fails at sources, before any shard, and the failure issue names that step
value.sourceDoesNotAnswer: noted in the summary and the night goes on, since the stand-in answers the shards either way
value.trustStoreMoved: the probe fails the shard as the harness, rather than every lookup failing as a finding
value.breakerOpened: the app skips that source for the cool-off after it comes back up, and app_stop then app_start resets it

backup-format-1.json with its plan and expected files, committed
a stand-in docker first on PATH, recording its argument list, for server_log, app_stop and app_start

GH_TOKEN and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set in the parent's environment when mcp.py starts under env -i, read back from /proc/<pid>/environ
every file under tools/nightly/, parsed for its imports
focus: the CA's private key must be shown to exist nowhere afterwards by listing both the output directory and the system's temporary directory, and the script must be made to fail mid-signing to show the key is still deleted. A check of the success path alone passes a key left behind by an error

every certificate field in the table must be read back from the certificate with openssl x509 -text, and the handshake must be shown to fail under any other server name. A handshake that succeeds under one name shows nothing about the name constraints or the SAN
the handshake test must use a default Python context, because that context enables X509_V_FLAG_X509_STRICT. A hand-built context with verification relaxed passes a certificate the image would refuse

known_table must equal the app's own /api/rates for the whole table on all four dates and three quotes, with the app's opener stubbed to answer from the stand-in's routing. Comparing known_table to itself, or to a hand-written figure, shows nothing about composition order or rounding
a source that is down must be recorded with mode: down and still answered 503. A stand-in that skips the record when down leaves qa blind to the very request that failed
seq must be shown to continue across a restart, and a malformed request must still be a line with every field. Asserting only the happy path passes a stand-in that logs after parsing
sources.py must be shown to classify 3xx as changed and 429 and 5xx as no-answer. The two sets differ by one status and an implementation that treats every non-200 alike passes half the table
probe's missing-route-out check must be run on the real nightly network. A probe that only reaches the stand-in passes when the network has a route out
prepare's refusals need a plan whose damaged record or pair is its holding's latest quantity, not only a plan missing a coverage name. The first would give two correct totals and no oracle

fixtures.mjs must be shown to write no record by its own crypto, which a request log cannot show. Assert the writes come through the served modules and that the damaged record and the pair alone use plant

every vault request the generator sends, the plant writes and makeStale's upgrade included, must be shown to carry X-Solvent-Vault, from a request capture of a fresh run. A generator that calls a raw fetch for the damaged record or the stale upgrade gets Bad Request from the gate and fails the night as the harness
no request to /api/rates in the run, asserted from the request log, since a lookup would spend the limit and reach the stand-in

after patch.py each vault's dashboard must show the manifest's display total under both pricing modes in a real browser, the damaged record must be reported unreadable, and the aged cookie must be refused as no session. Matching the rows alone passes data the screens cannot read

the idle-lock-out-of-range vault's decrypted profile record must hold idleLockMinutes: 0 and its Settings screen must show five minutes. A plan that stores 5, or a screen read that skips the stored value, passes a check of the screen alone

patch.py must be shown to change exactly the rows it names by dumping every table before and after and diffing every other table byte for byte, and to change nothing on an unknown key or a kdfMemory of 65536. A test of the updated rows alone misses a statement that reaches a table it should not

mcp.py must be shown to run docker with exactly the argument lists in the criteria, through a stand-in docker, and to refuse an extra argument, a wrong enum value and a malformed date without running anything. A schema that merely declares additionalProperties: false passes while the handler still reads the argument

the environment criterion must read /proc/<pid>/environ of the running server with the two tokens set in its parent. Reading os.environ from inside the process passes when a wrapper strips it after the fact

the import criterion must parse every file under tools/nightly/, Python and Node alike, and allow only the standard library, node: built-ins and the imports listed under Files (prices from standin.py, mcp.py and prices.py prepare, solvent.rates from sources.py, tests/browser/cdp.mjs from fixtures.mjs), and must also show no module under solvent/ imports from tools/. A rule that allowed any sibling import would pass a harness script reaching another script's internals
